cells.quote: The analysis revealed that community nurse training programs improved nurses' knowledge via hybrid pedagogical (SMD = 0.15–2.21), online (SMD = 0.12–0.29) and onsite methods (SMD = −0.51 to 0.11) and enhanced their skills through hybrid (SMD = 0.90) and onsite training (SMD = 0.44).
cells.note: Pooled evidence from six hybrid-training studies within the knowledge analysis; assessment points included immediate post-intervention and follow-up.

cells.quote: The online subgroup showed homogeneity and a small effect size (SMD = 0.21, 95% CI = 0.00, 0.42).
cells.note: The online subgroup comprised one study with four comparisons; the synthesis text describes a small effect.

cells.quote: However, no effects of the onsite subgroup were observed.
cells.note: The onsite subgroup included three studies; the study reports no observed effects rather than an equivalence result.

D.comparison: traditional machine-learning and standalone deep-learning models

cells.quote: Our proposed hybrid model, CNN-GRU, outperformed all baseline models. It achieved an accuracy of 73.08%, with a remarkable F1 score of 82.05%, demonstrating excellent performance in balancing precision (74%) and recall (91.18%).
cells.note: The comparison is between predictive models applied to fNIRS data, not randomly assigned learner conditions.

O.outcome_detail: Diagnostic image quality and procedural safety

cells.quote: An early study (Boulton et al. 1997) showed that clinical nurse specialists are capable of performing diagnostic cardiac catheterizations safely and effectively, producing high‐quality images without fatalities and with shorter procedure times.
cells.note: The study text reports the CNS outcome and statistical significance but does not specify the comparison group; the review table identifies the source as a nonrandomized retrospective study of 200 patients undergoing cardiac catheterization.
